packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-06: BLIND IMAGE READING (UNVERIFIED)

Exposure statement
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification of the work, author or a prior reading. I did not open packet.json, catalogues, editions or the web.
- The images themselves show a modern pencil shelfmark label on each face: "Stams, StA, Frg. 80-1r" (image-001/013, lower right) and "Stams, StA, Frg. 80-1v" (image-014/026). That is a holding label, not an identification of the text, and I have not used it for anything.
- Biblical and authority citations that are visible as written (e.g. "Joh 20", "Mat 20", "Ephes 6", "Gen 26", "Exo 12", "Reg 21", "Eccli 5", "Ps", "phys", "ethi") are transcribed from the leaf. Where I could only read part of a quotation, I have not filled it in from memory. In a few places I say a reading "matches" a familiar biblical phrase. Those are notes on the reading, not supplements.
- I did nothing beyond the rules. I listed the packet directory only to get the image filenames (packet.json appeared in that listing, and I did not open it).

Images
- image-001: overview, face A (labelled ...80-1r). image-002..013: tiles of face A (4 across x 3 down: 002-005 top, 006-009 middle, 010-013 bottom).
- image-014: overview, face B (labelled ...80-1v). image-015..026: tiles of face B, same grid (015-018 top, 019-022 middle, 023-026 bottom).
- All images loaded. The tiles overlap by several lines vertically and by a column edge horizontally. I counted repeated lines once.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- Bifolium of paper or soft parchment (horizontal chain/laid-type texture visible), photographed open, with a colour chart and scale. Damage at the fold: holes and losses along the central fold, and losses at the outer left edge of face A and the right edge of face B. These touch the margins, not the text block.
- Each leaf has two columns, so each face has four: a,b (left leaf) and c,d (right leaf). About 26-28 lines per column. Below the text there is a large blank lower margin.
- Script: small, cursive, heavily abbreviated late-medieval hand (Gothic cursiva/bastarda type). Red is used for rubrication (red strokes on capitals) and for red underlining of source citations and authority names.
- Rubrics in red:
  - Face A, col c: "D(omi)nica in Septuagesima", with a large red initial I hanging in the left margin.
  - Face B, col a: "D(omi)nica in Sexagesima", with a red initial A.
- Face A col a has a large red initial Q with a flourish, opening a new section about two-fifths of the way down.
- Marginalia:
  - A small note in the face A col b/c gutter, about 2/3 down: "1o"? or "fo"? (image-007/011, right).
  - Face A, lower margin under col b: "Dimitt(?) ar(?) / tc(?)", faint brown, perhaps a later pen trial or note (image-011, lower right).
  - Scattered interlinear superscript letters, which I read as abbreviation finishings, not glosses.
- The text appears to be continuous sermon-type prose: numbered divisions (primo, 2o, 3o; "De primo dicit..."), with biblical and authority citations underlined in red. I see no separation into lemma and commentary and no glossing layer.
- Physical continuity across faces (observation): face A col d ends "...quibus ipse dicit Ite" (image-013), and face B col a begins "et vos in vineam meam" (image-015). The right leaf of face A therefore backs onto the left leaf of face B. The Septuagesima section on face A (col c) is the one that continues on face B col a.

SELECTED SPANS
I attempted every column. Cols c and d of face A are the cleanest and are read fully. Face B col c and the upper half of face B col d are badly faded/abraded (a water-type stain), and are only partly read. Expansions are in ( ); "?" follows an uncertain reading; [illegible] marks text I could not read.

LIMITATIONS
- This is an unverified, first-pass image reading. The hand is very compressed, and many abbreviation marks are ambiguous (q(ui)/q(uia)/q(uod); p(ro)/p(er)/p(re)). The expansions are proposals.
- Face A col b, the first 6 lines of face B col a, face B col c lines 7-11, and face B col d lines 3-14 are heavily abraded or stained. My readings there are fragmentary, and should be rechecked at higher magnification or with raking/UV light.
- Several authority names in red underlining are uncertain: "Ar(istoteles)" vs "Aug(ustinus)" in face A col a line 7 and col c line 15, plus face A col b. Numerals in citations ("Job 28/3", "phys 2/4", "Reg 3 21") are also uncertain.
- Line numbers are counted from the first text line visible in each tile. Each tile repeats about 2-4 lines from the tile above, and I listed those lines only once.
- Column order on the bifolium is taken from the layout as photographed. The text continuity between face A col d and face B col a is an observation from the readings, not an assumption.
- Suggested next views:
  - Closer crops (2x) of face A col b top half (image-003 area) and face B col c/d upper halves (image-017/018 area).
  - Any image of the conjoint leaves or neighbouring fragments (Frg. 80-2 etc.), to establish what precedes face A col a and follows face B col d.
